The main object of this Act is to support the creation and retention of Australian jobs by:
requiring Australian Industry Participation plans for major projects; and
providing that an Australian Industry Participation plan for a major project will ensure that Australian entities have full, fair and reasonable opportunity to bid for:
the supply of key goods or services for the project; and
if the project involves establishing a new facility—the supply of key goods or services for the new facility’s initial operational phase.
The following is a simplified outline of this Act:
• An Australian Industry Participation plan (AIP plan) is required for a major project to establish, expand, improve or upgrade a facility.
• An AIP plan will deal with:
the project phase of a major project; and
if a major project involves establishing a new facility—the new facility’s initial operational phase.
• The key objective of an AIP plan is that Australian entities should have full, fair and reasonable opportunity to bid for:
the supply of key goods or services for the project; and
if the project involves establishing a new facility—the supply of key goods or services for the new facility’s initial operational phase.
• This Act sets up the Australian Industry Participation Authority.
• The Authority’s functions include:
approving AIP plans; and
monitoring compliance; and
other functions relating to Australian industry participation matters.
• The Minister may establish the Australian Industry Participation Advisory Board.

section.heading: Person responsible for carrying out project

content.p: Agreements
(1) If, under an agreement, a project, or a part of a project, is, or is to be, carried out by a person (the contractor) for and on behalf of another person, then, for the purposes of this Act:
the other person is taken to be the person responsible for carrying out the project, or the part of the project, as the case may be; and
the contractor is taken not to be responsible for carrying out the project, or the part of the project, as the case may be.
Subsection (1) has effect subject to subsections (3) and (5).

The Authority may, by writing, declare that, for the purposes of this Act:

section.heading: Key goods or services for a project

content.p: For the purposes of this Act, key goods or services are key goods or services for a project if, and only if, the goods or services are for use, wholly or partly, in connection with carrying out the project.

section.heading: Key goods or services for a new relevant facility’s initial operational phase

content.p: For the purposes of this Act, key goods or services are key goods or services for a new relevant facility’s initial operational phase if, and only if, the goods or services are for use, wholly or partly, in connection with the operation of the new relevant facility during the 2-year period starting when the establishment of the facility is completed.
(1) For the purposes of this Act, the trigger date for a project means:
if a trigger event for the project happens during the interim period—the first or only day during the interim period on which a trigger event for the project happens; or
if the earliest trigger event for the project happens on a day after the interim period—that day; or
if the Authority, by written notice given to the project proponent for the project, specifies another day—that other day.
Note 1: For trigger event, see subsection (4).
Note 2: For interim period, see subsection (5).
The Authority may specify a day under paragraph (1)(c):

on application made to the Authority by the project proponent for the project.
A day specified under paragraph (1)(c) must not be earlier than 120 days after the notice is given.
Trigger event
(4) For the purposes of this section, each of the following is a trigger event for a project:
block diagrams for the project are developed;
process flow diagrams for the project are developed;
a project proponent enters into a contract with another person under which the other person becomes a procurement entity in relation to the project;
a request for bids for the supply of key goods or services for the project is made;
technical specifications for the project are prepared;
a project proponent determines which standard or standards will apply to any of the key goods or services that are to be acquired for the project;
an equipment list for the project is prepared;
a project proponent first contacts a supplier with a request for pricing details for any of the key goods or services for the project;
a construction and contracting methodology for the project is developed;
an environmental submission is made in relation to the project;
a detailed schedule for the project is prepared;
a high-level scoping of the goods and services for the project is conducted.
Interim period
(5) For the purposes of this section, the interim period means the period:
beginning immediately after the end of the 90th day after the commencement of this section; and
ending 2 years after the commencement of this section.

section.heading: Extension to exclusive economic zone and continental shelf

content.p: This Act extends to a matter relating to the exercise of Australia’s sovereign rights in the exclusive economic zone or the continental shelf.

section.heading: Project proponent must give draft AIP plan to the Authority

content.p: The project proponent for a major project must give the Authority a draft AIP plan for the project:
at least 90 days before the trigger date for the project; or
if the Authority, by written notice given to the project proponent, specifies a later time—before that later time.
The Authority may specify a day under paragraph (1)(b):
on the Authority’s own initiative; or
on application made to the Authority by the project proponent for the project.
Subsection (1) does not apply if the project proponent is not aware that the project is a major project.
If:
no draft AIP plan for a major project has been given under subsection (1); and
a draft AIP plan would have been required to have been given under subsection (1) if the project proponent for the project had been aware that the project was a major project; and
the project proponent for the project becomes aware that the project is a major project;
the project proponent for the project must:
give the Authority a draft AIP plan for the project; and
do so within 60 days after becoming so aware.
Exceptions
This section does not apply to the project proponent if the project proponent has prepared a plan that:
has been given to a State or Territory; and
complies with the conditions specified in the legislative rules.
This section does not apply to the project proponent if the conditions specified in the legislative rules are satisfied.
If the project proponent for a major project gives the Authority a draft AIP plan for the project under section 17, the Authority must:
approve the plan; or
refuse to approve the plan.
Approval of plan
The Authority must not approve a draft AIP plan under subsection (1) unless:
the draft AIP plan complies with the AIP plan rules; and
the Authority is satisfied that the steps specified in accordance with subsections 35(2), 36(2), 39(2) and 40(2) are adequate.
If the Authority approves the draft AIP plan under subsection (1), the plan becomes the approved AIP plan for the project.
If the Authority approves the draft AIP plan under subsection (1), the Authority must give the project proponent a written notice setting out the decision.
Refusal to approve plan—direction to give revised plan
If the Authority refuses to approve the draft AIP plan under subsection (1), the Authority must, by written notice given to the project proponent, direct the project proponent to:
give the Authority a revised draft AIP plan that:
complies with the AIP plan rules; and
sets out adequate steps specified in accordance with subsections 35(2), 36(2), 39(2) and 40(2); and
do so within 30 days after the notice is given.
The project proponent must comply with a direction under subsection (5).
Approval of revised plan
If:
the project proponent for a major project gives the Authority a revised draft AIP plan for the project; and
the revised draft AIP plan is given as a result of a direction under subsection (5); and
the revised draft AIP plan complies with that direction;
the Authority must approve the revised draft AIP plan.
If the Authority approves the revised draft AIP plan under subsection (7), the plan becomes the approved AIP plan for the project.
If the Authority approves the revised draft AIP plan under subsection (7), the Authority must give the project proponent a written notice setting out the decision.
Timing
The Authority must take all reasonable steps to ensure that a decision is made on a draft AIP plan for a project within 30 days after the Authority is given the draft AIP plan.

section.heading: Replacement of approved AIP plan before completion of project

content.p: If:
(a) an approved AIP plan (the original plan) for a major project is in force; and
the project has not been completed;
the project proponent for the project may give the Authority a draft AIP plan that is expressed to replace the original plan.
If the project proponent gives the Authority a draft AIP plan for the project under subsection (1), the Authority must:
approve the plan; or
refuse to approve the plan.
Approval of replacement plan
The Authority must not approve a draft AIP plan under subsection (2) unless:
the draft AIP plan complies with the AIP plan rules; and
the Authority is satisfied that the steps specified in accordance with subsections 35(2), 36(2), 39(2) and 40(2) are adequate.
If the Authority approves the draft AIP plan under subsection (2), the plan becomes the approved AIP plan for the project.
If the draft AIP plan becomes the approved AIP plan for the project, the original plan ceases to be in force.
Notice of decision
If the Authority approves the draft AIP plan under subsection (2), the Authority must give the project proponent a written notice setting out the decision.
If the Authority refuses to approve the draft AIP plan under subsection (2), the Authority must give the project proponent a written notice setting out the decision.
Timing
The Authority must take all reasonable steps to ensure that a decision is made on a draft AIP plan for a project within 30 days after the Authority is given the draft AIP plan.

section.heading: Replacement of approved AIP plan after completion of project

content.p: If:
(a) an approved AIP plan (the original plan) for a major project is in force; and
the project involves establishing a new relevant facility; and
the project has been completed;
the operator of the new relevant facility may give the Authority a draft AIP plan:
that is expressed to replace the original plan; and
Part B of which is identical to Part B of the original plan.
Note: Section 30 deals with Parts of AIP plans.
If the operator gives the Authority a draft AIP plan for the project under subsection (1), the Authority must:
approve the plan; or
refuse to approve the plan.
Approval of replacement plan
The Authority must not approve a draft AIP plan under subsection (2) unless:
the draft AIP plan complies with the AIP plan rules (other than Subdivision C of Division 2); and
the Authority is satisfied that steps specified in accordance with subsections 39(2) and 40(2) are adequate.
If the Authority approves the draft AIP plan under subsection (2), the plan becomes the approved AIP plan for the project.
If the draft AIP plan becomes the approved AIP plan for the project, the original plan ceases to be in force.
Notice of decision
If the Authority approves the draft AIP plan under subsection (2), the Authority must give the operator a written notice setting out the decision.
If the Authority refuses to approve the draft AIP plan under subsection (2), the Authority must give the operator a written notice setting out the decision.
Timing
The Authority must take all reasonable steps to ensure that a decision is made on a draft AIP plan for a project within 30 days after the Authority is given the draft AIP plan.
Project involves establishing a new relevant facility
If a major project involves establishing a new relevant facility, an approved AIP plan for the project:
comes into force when the Authority approves the plan; and
subject to this Division, continues in force until the end of the 2-year period beginning when the project is completed.
Project does not involve establishing a new relevant facility
If a major project does not involve establishing a new relevant facility, an approved AIP plan for the project:
comes into force when the Authority approves the plan; and
subject to this Division, continues in force until the project is completed.

If a person gives the Authority a draft AIP plan for a major project, the person must also give the Authority a summary of the steps specified in accordance with whichever of subsections 35(2), 36(2), 39(2) and 40(2) are applicable.
The summary must be in a form approved, in writing, by the Authority.
The Authority must ensure that the summary is available on the Authority’s website throughout the 15-day period beginning on the day after the summary was received by the Authority.

section.heading: Project proponent must notify estimated completion date for a new relevant facility

content.p: If:
the project proponent for a major project gives a draft AIP plan for the project to the Authority; and
the project involves establishing a new relevant facility; and
the establishment of the facility has not been completed;
the project proponent must:
notify the Authority of the estimated date of completion of the establishment of the facility; and
do so at or about the same time as the draft AIP plan is given to the Authority.
A notification under subsection (1) must be in a form approved, in writing, by the Authority.
The Authority must maintain a register in which the Authority includes all approved AIP plans that are in force.
The register may be kept in electronic form.
Project proponent
If an approved AIP plan for a major project is in force, the project proponent for the major project must comply with Part B of the plan.
Note: Section 30 deals with Parts of AIP plans.
Operator of new relevant facility
If:
an approved AIP plan for a major project is in force; and
the project involves establishing a new relevant facility;
the operator of the new relevant facility must comply with Part C of the plan.
Note: Section 30 deals with Parts of AIP plans.
Scope
This section applies to a major project if an approved AIP plan for the project is, or has been, in force.
Reporting period
(2) For the purposes of this section, a reporting period for the plan is:
the period of 6 months beginning on the day on which the plan is approved; and
each subsequent 6-month period during any part of which:
the plan is in force; and
the project proponent for the project is subject to any obligations under Part B of the plan.
Note: Section 30 deals with Parts of AIP plans.
Subsection (2) has effect subject to subsection (4).

(4) The Authority may, by written notice given to the project proponent for the project, determine that, for the purposes of this section, a reporting period for the plan has the meaning given by the determination.
A determination under subsection (4) is not a legislative instrument.
Compliance report—project proponent

The project proponent for the project must, within 3 months after the end of each reporting period, prepare and give the Authority a report relating to compliance with Part B of the plan during the reporting period.
Note: Section 30 deals with Parts of AIP plans.
A report under subsection (6) must:
be in a form approved, in writing, by the Authority; and
(b) be accompanied by such information as is specified in the legislative rules.

section.heading: Compliance report—operator of new relevant facility

content.p: Scope
This section applies to a major project if:
an approved AIP plan for the project is, or has been, in force; and
the project involves establishing a new relevant facility.
Reporting period
(2) For the purposes of this section, a reporting period for the plan is:
the period of 6 months beginning on the day on which the plan is approved; and
each subsequent 6-month period during any part of which:
the plan is in force; and
the operator of the new relevant facility is subject to any obligations under Part C of the plan.
Note: Section 30 deals with Parts of AIP plans.
Compliance report—operator of new relevant facility

The operator of the new relevant facility must, within 3 months after the end of each reporting period, prepare and give the Authority a report relating to compliance with Part C of the plan during the reporting period.
A report under subsection (3) must:
be in a form approved, in writing, by the Authority; and
(b) be accompanied by such information as is specified in the legislative rules.
If an approved AIP plan is, or has been, in force for a major project, the project proponent for the project must:
keep such records as are reasonably necessary to enable the Authority to ascertain whether Part B of the plan has been complied with; and
retain those records for 5 years.
Note: Section 30 deals with Parts of AIP plans.
If:
an approved AIP plan is, or has been, in force for a major project; and
the project involves establishing a new relevant facility;
the operator of the new relevant facility must:
keep such records as are reasonably necessary to enable the Authority to ascertain whether Part C of the plan has been complied with; and
retain those records for 5 years.
Note: Section 30 deals with Parts of AIP plans.
Subdivision A—General rules
This Division sets out the AIP plan rules.
If a major project involves establishing a new relevant facility, an AIP plan for the project must be divided into the following Parts:
Part A—Title;
Part B—Project Phase;
Part C—Initial Facility Operational Phase.
If a major project does not involve establishing a new relevant facility, an AIP plan for the project must be divided into the following Parts:
Part A—Title;
Part B—Project Phase.

section.heading: AIP plan must be in the approved form

content.p: An AIP plan must be in a form approved, in writing, by the Authority.
Subdivision B—Rule for Part A of the plan (Title)
Part A of an AIP plan for a major project must state that the plan is the AIP plan for the project.
Subdivision C—Rules for Part B of the plan (Project Phase)

section.heading: Part B of AIP plan binds project proponent

content.p: Part B of an AIP plan for a major project must state that Part B of the plan binds the project proponent for the project from time to time.

Part B of an AIP plan for a major project must state that the key objective of Part B of the plan is that Australian entities should have full, fair and reasonable opportunity to bid for the supply of key goods or services for the project.

Part B of an AIP plan for a major project must state that, until the project is completed, the project proponent for the project will take all reasonable steps to ensure that each procurement entity for the project will achieve the following objectives:
the key objective of Part B of the plan;
the objective that the procurement entity will have a publicly accessible website;

the objective that the procurement entity will not request bids to supply key goods or services for the project unless the procurement entity has a broad understanding of the capability and capacity of Australian entities generally to supply those goods or services;
the objective that requirements that potential bidders must satisfy in order to bid to supply key goods or services for the project:
will be published on the website of the procurement entity; and
will be so published at a reasonable time before the request for bids is made;
the objective that:
standards for key goods or services for the project that are to be acquired by the procurement entity will be published on the website of the procurement entity; and

if the standards are neither Australian standards nor international standards—the procurement entity will publish on its website a statement explaining why neither Australian standards nor international standards are being used;

the objective that the procurement entity will not discriminate against Australian entities in relation to timeframes for responding to requests for bids to supply key goods or services for the project;
the objective that the procurement entity will:
provide feedback to Australian entities whose bids to supply key goods or services for the project have not been successful; and
ensure that such feedback includes recommendations about any relevant training and any relevant skills capability and capacity development;
the objective that the procurement entity will:
at all times have an employee who is designated as the procurement contact officer for the project; and
publish the procurement contact officer’s contact details on the procurement entity’s website.

Part B of an AIP plan must state that, until the project is completed, the project proponent will take specified steps directed towards ensuring that the objectives set out in subsection (1) are achieved by each procurement entity for the project.
Part B of an AIP plan for a major project must state that, until the project is completed, the project proponent for the project will:
have a publicly accessible website; and
conduct awareness programs about opportunities for Australian entities to supply key goods or services for the project; and
conduct training programs that are:
for employees of procurement entities for the project; and
directed towards ensuring that the objectives set out in section 35 are achieved; and
publish on its website a statement of the proponent’s expectations in relation to:
(i) key goods or services that are likely to be acquired for the project; and
opportunities for Australian entities to supply key goods or services for the project; and
opportunities for non-Australian entities to supply key goods or services for the project;
broken down into categories of goods or services in the way specified in the legislative rules; and
both:
cause to be published on a publicly accessible website statements about available opportunities to supply key goods or services for the project; and
notify the Authority of the URL of the website; and
if the project proponent has a global supply chain—encourage Australian entities that are supplying, or have supplied, key goods or services for the project to:
develop the capability and capacity to supply key goods or services to the project proponent’s global supply chain; and
integrate into the project proponent’s global supply chain; and
both:
at all times have an employee who is designated as the project proponent’s contact officer for the purposes of this Act; and
notify the Authority of the contact officer’s contact details.
Part B of an AIP plan must state that, until the project is completed, the project proponent will take specified steps directed towards the fulfilment of the obligations set out in subsection (1).
Subdivision D—Rules for Part C of the plan (Initial Facility Operational Phase)

section.heading: Part C of the plan binds operator of new relevant facility

content.p: Part C of an AIP plan for a major project must state that Part C of the plan binds the operator of the new relevant facility from time to time.

Part C of an AIP plan for a major project must state that the key objective of Part C of the plan is that Australian entities should have full, fair and reasonable opportunity to bid for the supply of key goods or services for the new relevant facility’s initial operational phase.

section.heading: Primary obligations of operator of new relevant facility

content.p: Part C of an AIP plan for a major project must state that the operator of the new relevant facility will take all reasonable steps to ensure that each procurement entity for the new relevant facility will achieve the following objectives:
the key objective of Part C of the plan;
the objective that the procurement entity will have a publicly accessible website;

the objective that the procurement entity will not request bids to supply key goods or services for the new relevant facility’s initial operational phase unless the procurement entity has a broad understanding of the capability and capacity of Australian entities generally to supply those goods or services;
the objective that requirements that potential bidders must satisfy in order to bid to supply key goods or services for the new relevant facility’s initial operational phase:
will be published on the website of the procurement entity; and
will be so published at a reasonable time before the request for bids is made;
the objective that:

standards for key goods or services that are to be acquired for the new relevant facility’s initial operational phase by the procurement entity will be published on the website of the procurement entity; and

if the standards are neither Australian standards nor international standards—the procurement entity will publish on its website a statement explaining why neither Australian standards nor international standards are being used;

the objective that the procurement entity will not discriminate against Australian entities in relation to timeframes for responding to requests for bids to supply key goods or services for the new relevant facility’s initial operational phase;
the objective that the procurement entity will:
provide feedback to Australian entities whose bids to supply key goods or services for the new relevant facility’s initial operational phase have not been successful; and
ensure that such feedback includes recommendations about any relevant training and any relevant skills capability and capacity development;
the objective that the procurement entity will:
at all times have an employee who is designated as the procurement contact officer for the new relevant facility; and
publish the procurement contact officer’s contact details on the procurement entity’s website.

Part C of an AIP plan must state that the operator of the new relevant facility will take specified steps directed towards ensuring that the objectives set out in subsection (1) are achieved by each procurement entity for the new relevant facility.

section.heading: Other obligations of operator of new relevant facility

content.p: Part C of an AIP plan for a major project must state that the operator of the new relevant facility will:
have a publicly accessible website; and
conduct awareness programs about opportunities for Australian entities to supply key goods or services for the new relevant facility’s initial operational phase; and
conduct training programs that are:
for employees of procurement entities for the new relevant facility; and
directed towards ensuring that the objectives set out in section 39 are achieved; and
publish on its website a statement of the operator’s expectations in relation to:
(i) key goods or services that are likely to be acquired for the new relevant facility’s initial operational phase; and
opportunities for Australian entities to supply key goods or services for the new relevant facility’s initial operational phase; and
opportunities for non-Australian entities to supply key goods or services for the new relevant facility’s initial operational phase;
broken down into categories of goods or services in the way specified in the legislative rules; and
both:
cause to be published on a publicly accessible website statements about available opportunities to supply key goods or services for the new relevant facility’s initial operational phase; and
notify the Authority of the URL of the website; and
if the operator has a global supply chain—encourage Australian entities that are supplying, or have supplied, key goods or services for the new relevant facility’s initial operational phase to:
develop the capability and capacity to supply key goods or services to the operator’s global supply chain; and
integrate into the operator’s global supply chain; and
both:
at all times have an employee who is designated as the operator’s contact officer for the purposes of this Act; and
notify the Authority of the contact officer’s contact details.
Part C of an AIP plan must state that the operator of the new relevant facility will take specified steps directed towards the fulfilment of the obligations set out in subsection (1).

section.heading: Authority to be notified of preliminary trigger day for major project

content.p: If:
the preliminary trigger day for a designated project occurs after the commencement of this section; and
at any time on the preliminary trigger day, the project proponent for the project was aware that it was reasonably likely that the project would be a major project;
the project proponent must:
notify the Authority of the preliminary trigger day; and
do so within 60 days after the preliminary trigger day.
If:
the preliminary trigger day for a designated project occurs after the commencement of this section; and
the project proponent for the project was not aware, at any time on the preliminary trigger day, that it was reasonably likely that the project would be a major project; and
the project proponent becomes aware that the project is, or is reasonably likely to be, a major project;
the project proponent must:
notify the Authority of the preliminary trigger day; and
(e) do so within 14 days after becoming so aware.
A notification under this section must:
be in a form approved, in writing, by the Authority; and
be accompanied by such information as is specified in the legislative rules; and
be accompanied by such documents (if any) as are specified in the legislative rules.
Preliminary trigger day
(4) For the purposes of this section, the preliminary trigger day for a project means the day on which the earliest of the following events happens:
the project concept design begins;
an environmental assessment begins to be carried out by a project proponent;
a project proponent enters into a contract with another person to carry out an environmental assessment of the project;
the raw materials for the project are estimated;
the utility consumption for the project is estimated.

section.heading: Person must notify Authority if the person becomes a project proponent for a major project

content.p: If a person becomes a project proponent for a major project, the person must:
notify the Authority that the person has become a project proponent for the project; and
do so within 60 days after becoming a project proponent.
A notification under subsection (1) must:
be in a form approved, in writing, by the Authority; and
(b) be accompanied by such information as is specified in the legislative rules.

section.heading: Person must notify Authority if the person ceases to be a project proponent for a major project

content.p: If a person ceases to be a project proponent for a major project, the person must:
notify the Authority of the cessation; and
do so within 60 days after the cessation occurs.
A notification under subsection (1) must:
be in a form approved, in writing, by the Authority; and
(b) be accompanied by such information as is specified in the legislative rules.

section.heading: Project proponent must notify Authority if major project is abandoned or cancelled

content.p: If a major project is abandoned or cancelled, the project proponent for the project must:
notify the Authority of the abandonment or cancellation; and
do so within 60 days after the project is abandoned or cancelled.
A notification under subsection (1) must:
be in a form approved, in writing, by the Authority; and
(b) be accompanied by such information as is specified in the legislative rules.

section.heading: Project proponent must notify Authority of certain events

content.p: If:
a person is the project proponent for a major project; and
a notifiable event occurs;
the person must:
notify the Authority of the event; and
do so within 60 days after the event occurs.
A notification under subsection (1) must:
be in a form approved, in writing, by the Authority; and
(b) be accompanied by such information as is specified in the legislative rules.
(3) The legislative rules may declare that a specified event is a notifiable event for the purposes of this section.

section.heading: Person must notify Authority if the person becomes an operator of new relevant facility

content.p: If:
a major project involves establishing a new relevant facility; and
a person becomes an operator of the new relevant facility;
the person must:
notify the Authority; and
do so within 60 days after becoming an operator.
A notification under subsection (1) must:
be in a form approved, in writing, by the Authority; and
(b) be accompanied by such information as is specified in the legislative rules.

section.heading: Person must notify Authority if the person ceases to be an operator of new relevant facility

content.p: If:
a major project involves establishing a new relevant facility; and
a person ceases to be an operator of the new relevant facility;
the person must:
notify the Authority of the cessation; and
do so within 60 days after the cessation occurs.
A notification under subsection (1) must:
be in a form approved, in writing, by the Authority; and
(b) be accompanied by such information as is specified in the legislative rules.

section.heading: Operator of new relevant facility must notify Authority of certain events

content.p: If:
a major project involves establishing a new relevant facility; and
a notifiable event occurs;
the operator of the new relevant facility must:
notify the Authority of the event; and
do so within 60 days after the event occurs.
A notification under subsection (1) must:
be in a form approved, in writing, by the Authority; and
(b) be accompanied by such information as is specified in the legislative rules.
(3) The legislative rules may declare that a specified event is a notifiable event for the purposes of this section.

section.heading: Authority may obtain information or documents

content.p: Scope
This section applies to a person if the Authority believes on reasonable grounds that the person has information or a document that is relevant to the operation of this Act.
Requirement
The Authority may, by written notice given to the person, require the person to:
give to the Authority, within the period and in the manner and form specified in the notice, any such information; or
produce to the Authority, within the period and in the manner specified in the notice, any such documents; or
make copies of any such documents and to produce to the Authority, within the period and in the manner specified in the notice, those copies.
A period specified under subsection (2) must not be shorter than 14 days after the notice is given.
Compliance
A person must comply with a requirement under subsection (2) to the extent that the person is capable of doing so.
A person is entitled to be paid by the Commonwealth reasonable compensation for complying with a requirement covered by paragraph 50(2)(c).
The Authority may:
inspect a document or copy produced under subsection 50(2); and
make and retain copies of, or take and retain extracts from, such a document.
The Authority may retain possession of a copy of a document produced in accordance with a requirement covered by paragraph 50(2)(c).
The Authority may take, and retain for as long as is necessary, possession of a document produced under subsection 50(2).
The person otherwise entitled to possession of the document is entitled to be supplied, as soon as practicable, with a copy certified by the Authority to be a true copy.
The certified copy must be received in all courts and tribunals as evidence as if it were the original.

Until a certified copy is supplied, the Authority must, at such times and places as the Authority thinks appropriate, permit the person otherwise entitled to possession of the document, or a person authorised by that person, to inspect and make copies of, or take extracts from, the document.

An individual is excused from giving information or producing a document under section 50 on the ground that the information or the production of the document might tend to incriminate the individual or expose the individual to a penalty.

division.heading: Powers to obtain information from project proponent

section.heading: Authority may obtain information from project proponent

content.p: Scope
This section applies to the project proponent for a major project if an approved AIP plan is, or has been, in force for the project.
Requirement
The Authority may, by written notice given to the project proponent, require the proponent to:
give to the Authority such information relating to the project as is specified in the notice; and
do so within the period and in the manner and form specified in the notice.
A period specified under paragraph (2)(b) must not be shorter than 14 days after the notice is given.
Compliance
A person must comply with a requirement under subsection (2) to the extent that the person is capable of doing so.
Self-incrimination
An individual is excused from giving information under this section on the ground that the information might tend to incriminate the individual or expose the individual to a penalty.
General information-gathering power not limited
This section does not, by implication, limit section 50.

division.heading: Powers to obtain information from operator of facility

section.heading: Authority may obtain information from operator of new relevant facility

content.p: Scope
If:
an approved AIP plan is, or has been, in force for a major project; and
the project involves establishing a new relevant facility;
this section applies to the operator of the new relevant facility.
Requirement
The Authority may, by written notice given to the operator, require the operator to:
give to the Authority such information relating to the operation of the new relevant facility as is specified in the notice; and
do so within the period and in the manner and form specified in the notice.
A period specified under paragraph (2)(b) must not be shorter than 14 days after the notice is given.
Compliance
A person must comply with a requirement under subsection (2) to the extent that the person is capable of doing so.
Self-incrimination
An individual is excused from giving information under this section on the ground that the information might tend to incriminate the individual or expose the individual to a penalty.
General information-gathering power not limited
This section does not, by implication, limit section 50.
Scope
(1) This section applies if a person (the relevant person), without reasonable excuse, contravenes Part 2, 3 or 4.
Adverse publicity notice
The Authority may, by written notice given to the relevant person, require the relevant person to:
take either or both of the following actions within the period specified in the notice:
to publicise, in the way specified in the notice, the contravention, the details of the contravention, and any other related matter;
to notify a specified person or specified class of person, in the way specified in the notice, of the contravention, the details of the contravention, and any other related matter; and
give the Authority, within 7 days after the end of the period specified in the notice, evidence that the action or actions were taken by the relevant person in accordance with the notice.
If the relevant person is a subsidiary of a constitutional corporation, the Authority may, by written notice given to the corporation, require the corporation to:
take either or both of the following actions within the period specified in the notice:

to publicise, in the way specified in the notice, the name of the relevant person, the relevant person’s contravention, the details of the contravention, the fact that the relevant person is a subsidiary of the corporation, and any other related matter;

to notify a specified person or specified class of person, in the way specified in the notice, of the relevant person’s contravention, the details of the contravention, the fact that the relevant person is a subsidiary of the corporation, and any other related matter; and
give the Authority, within 7 days after the end of the period specified in the notice, evidence that the action or actions were taken by the corporation in accordance with the notice.
Naming relevant person etc. in annual report
The Authority may, in a report under section 83:
name the relevant person as having contravened Part 2, 3 or 4, and set out details of the contravention; and
if the relevant person is a subsidiary of a body corporate—name the relevant person as a subsidiary of the body corporate.
Naming relevant person etc. in other ways
The Authority may, by electronic or other means:
name the relevant person as having contravened Part 2, 3 or 4, and set out details of the contravention; and
if the relevant person is a subsidiary of a body corporate—name the relevant person as a subsidiary of the body corporate.
Prior notice to relevant person etc.
If the Authority proposes to:
give a notice to a person under subsection (2) or (3); or
name a person in a report in accordance with subsection (4); or
name a person under subsection (5);
the Authority must:
give the person notice in writing of the proposal and the reasons for the proposal; and
invite the person to:
make written representations to the Authority about the proposal; and
do so within the period of 28 days beginning on the day specified in the notice; and
have regard to any written representations made by the person within that period.
Restraining injunctions
If a person has engaged, is engaging or is proposing to engage in any conduct in contravention of Part 2, 3 or 4, a prescribed court may, on the application of the Authority, grant an injunction:
restraining the person from engaging in the conduct; and
if, in the court’s opinion, it is desirable to do so—requiring the person to do something.
Performance injunctions
If:
a person has refused or failed, or is refusing or failing, or is proposing to refuse or fail, to do an act or thing; and
the refusal or failure was, is or would be a contravention of Part 2, 3 or 4;
a prescribed court may, on the application of the Authority, grant an injunction requiring the person to do that act or thing.
Grant of interim injunction

If an application is made to a prescribed court for an injunction under section 58, the court may, before considering the application, grant an interim injunction restraining a person from engaging in conduct of a kind referred to in that section.
No undertakings as to damages
A prescribed court is not to require the Authority, as a condition of granting an interim injunction, to give any undertakings as to damages.
A prescribed court may discharge or vary an injunction granted under this Division.

section.heading: Certain limits on granting injunctions not to apply

content.p: Restraining injunctions
The power of a prescribed court under this Division to grant an injunction restraining a person from engaging in conduct of a particular kind may be exercised:

if the court is satisfied that the person has engaged in conduct of that kind—whether or not it appears to the court that the person intends to engage again, or to continue to engage, in conduct of that kind; or

if it appears to the court that, if an injunction is not granted, it is likely that the person will engage in conduct of that kind—whether or not the person has previously engaged in conduct of that kind.
Performance injunctions
The power of a prescribed court under this Division to grant an injunction requiring a person to do an act or thing may be exercised:

if the court is satisfied that the person has refused or failed to do that act or thing—whether or not it appears to the court that the person intends to refuse or fail again, or to continue to refuse or fail, to do that act or thing; or

if it appears to the court that, if an injunction is not granted, it is likely that the person will refuse or fail to do that act or thing—whether or not the person has previously refused or failed to do that act or thing.

section.heading: Other powers of the court unaffected

content.p: The powers conferred on a prescribed court under this Division are in addition to, and not instead of, any other powers of the court, whether conferred by this Act or otherwise.

part.heading: Multiple project proponents and multiple facility operators

content.p: If there are 2 or more persons (the multiple project proponents) who have joint or several responsibility for carrying out a project, or a part of a project, then:
for the purposes of this Act, each of the multiple project proponents is a project proponent for the project; and
a reference in:
this Act; or
the legislative rules; or
another instrument made under this Act; or
an approved AIP plan; or
a draft AIP plan;
to the project proponent for the project is to be read as a reference to each of the multiple project proponents.
Scope
This section applies if:
(a) there are 2 or more project proponents (the multiple project proponents) for a project; and
either of the following:
this Act;
an approved AIP plan for the project;
imposes an obligation on the project proponent for the project.
Obligations of project proponent
The obligation is imposed on each of the multiple project proponents, but may be discharged by any of the multiple project proponents.

section.heading: References to operators of new relevant facilities

content.p: If:
a major project involves establishing a new relevant facility; and
(b) there are 2 or more persons (the multiple operators) who have, or are to have, joint or several responsibility for operating the new relevant facility, or a part of the new relevant facility;
then:
for the purposes of this Act, each of the multiple operators is an operator of the new relevant facility; and
a reference in:
this Act; or
the legislative rules; or
another instrument made under this Act; or
an approved AIP plan; or
a draft AIP plan;
to the operator of the new relevant facility is to be read as a reference to each of the multiple operators.

section.heading: Obligations of multiple operators of new relevant facility

content.p: Scope
This section applies if:
a major project involves establishing a new relevant facility; and
(b) there are 2 or more operators (the multiple operators) of the new relevant facility; and
either of the following:
this Act;
an approved AIP plan for the project;
imposes an obligation on the operator of the facility.
Obligations of operators

The obligation is imposed on each of the multiple operators, but, if the multiple operators have, or are to have, joint responsibility for operating the new relevant facility, the obligation may be discharged by any of the multiple operators.

division.heading: Office and functions of the Australian Industry Participation Authority

section.heading: Establishment of the Australian Industry Participation Authority

content.p: There is to be an Australian Industry Participation Authority.
Note: In this Act, Authority means the Australian Industry Participation Authority (see section 5).
The functions of the Authority are:
such functions as are conferred on the Authority by this Act; and
to advise and assist persons in relation to their obligations under this Act; and
to monitor compliance with this Act; and
to promote compliance with this Act; and
to collect, analyse, interpret and disseminate information relating to AIP matters; and
to support, encourage, conduct and evaluate training programs that are directed towards improving the skills and knowledge of people involved in AIP matters; and
to support, encourage, conduct and evaluate educational, promotional and community awareness programs that are relevant to AIP matters; and
to support, encourage, conduct and evaluate research about AIP matters; and
to advise the Minister about AIP matters; and
to consult and cooperate with other persons, organisations and governments on AIP matters; and
on behalf of the Commonwealth, to administer such schemes and programs as are specified in the legislative rules; and
such functions as are conferred on the Authority by a law other than this Act; and
such other functions (if any) as are specified in the legislative rules; and
to do anything incidental to or conducive to the performance of any of the above functions.
Section 3 does not, by implication, limit subsection (1).
The Authority is to be appointed by the Minister by written instrument.
A person is not eligible for appointment as the Authority unless the Minister is satisfied that the person has:
substantial experience or knowledge; and
significant standing;
in at least one of the following fields:
economics;
industry;
public administration.
The Authority holds office on a full-time basis.

section.heading: Period of appointment for the Authority

content.p: The Authority holds office for the period specified in the instrument of appointment. The period must not exceed 5 years.
Note: The Authority may be reappointed: see the Acts Interpretation Act 1901.
The Minister may appoint a person to act as the Authority:
during a vacancy in the office of the Authority (whether or not an appointment has previously been made to the office); or
during any period, or during all periods, when the Authority:
is absent from duty or from Australia; or
is, for any reason, unable to perform the duties of the office.
Note: For rules that apply to acting appointments, see section 33A of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901.
A person is not eligible for appointment to act as the Authority unless the person is eligible for appointment as the Authority.

division.heading: Terms and conditions for the Authority

content.p: The Authority is to be paid the remuneration that is determined by the Remuneration Tribunal. If no determination of that remuneration by the Tribunal is in operation, the Authority is to be paid the remuneration that is prescribed by the legislative rules.
The Authority is to be paid the allowances that are prescribed by the legislative rules.
(3) This section has effect subject to the Remuneration Tribunal Act 1973.
The Authority has the recreation leave entitlements that are determined by the Remuneration Tribunal.
The Minister may grant the Authority leave of absence, other than recreation leave, on the terms and conditions as to remuneration or otherwise that the Minister determines.
The Authority must not engage in paid employment outside the duties of his or her office without the Minister’s approval.

section.heading: Disclosure of interests to the Minister

content.p: The Authority must give written notice to the Minister of all interests, pecuniary or otherwise, that the Authority has or acquires and that conflict or could conflict with the proper performance of the Authority’s functions.
The Authority may resign his or her appointment by giving the Minister a written resignation.
The resignation takes effect on the day it is received by the Minister or, if a later day is specified in the resignation, on that later day.
The Minister may terminate the appointment of the Authority:
for misbehaviour; or
if the Authority is unable to perform the duties of his or her office because of physical or mental incapacity.
The Minister may terminate the appointment of the Authority if:
the Authority:
becomes bankrupt; or
applies to take the benefit of any law for the relief of bankrupt or insolvent debtors; or
compounds with his or her creditors; or
makes an assignment of his or her remuneration for the benefit of his or her creditors; or
the Authority is absent, except on leave of absence, for 14 consecutive days or for 28 days in any 12 months; or
the Authority engages, except with the Minister’s approval, in paid employment outside the duties of his or her office (see section 74); or
the Authority fails, without reasonable excuse, to comply with section 75.
The Authority holds office on the terms and conditions (if any) in relation to matters not covered by this Act that are determined by the Minister.
The Authority may, by writing, delegate any or all of the Authority’s functions or powers to:
an SES employee; or
an acting SES employee; or
an APS employee who holds or performs the duties of:
an Executive Level 2 position; or
an equivalent position.
Note: The expressions SES employee and acting SES employee are defined in the Acts Interpretation Act 1901.
A delegate must comply with any written directions of the Authority.
The staff assisting the Authority are to be persons engaged under the Public Service Act 1999 and made available for the purpose by the Secretary of the Department.
The Authority may also be assisted:
(a) by officers and employees of Agencies (within the meaning of the Public Service Act 1999); or
by officers and employees of authorities of the Commonwealth; or
by officers and employees of a State or Territory; or
by officers and employees of authorities of a State or Territory;
whose services are made available to the Authority in connection with the performance of any of the Authority’s functions.
The Authority may, on behalf of the Commonwealth, engage persons having suitable qualifications and experience as consultants to the Authority.
The consultants are to be engaged on the terms and conditions that the Authority determines in writing.

The Authority must, as soon as practicable after the end of each financial year, prepare and give to the Minister, for presentation to the Parliament, a report on the operations of the Authority during that year.
Note: See also section 34C of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901, which contains extra rules about annual reports.

section.heading: Minister may give directions to the Authority

content.p: The Minister may, by legislative instrument, give directions to the Authority about the performance of the Authority’s functions.
Note 1: For variation and revocation, see the Acts Interpretation Act 1901.

Note 2: Section 42 (disallowance) and Part 4 of Chapter 3 (sunsetting) of the Legislation Act 2003 do not apply to the direction (see regulations made for the purposes of paragraphs 44(2)(b) and 54(2)(b) of that Act).
A direction under subsection (1) must be of a general nature only.
The Authority must comply with a direction under subsection (1).

section.heading: Establishment of Australian Industry Participation Advisory Board

content.p: The Minister may, by writing, establish a committee to be known as the Australian Industry Participation Advisory Board.
Note: In this Act, AIP advisory board means the Australian Industry Participation Advisory Board (see section 5).
Before establishing the AIP advisory board, the Minister must consult the Authority.
An instrument made under subsection (1) is not a legislative instrument.
The AIP advisory board has the following functions:
to advise the Authority, at the Authority’s request, about matters relating to the performance of the Authority’s functions;
to advise the Minister, at the Minister’s request, about AIP matters;
to do anything incidental to or conducive to the performance of either of the above functions.

division.heading: Appointment etc. of AIP advisory board members

content.p: The AIP advisory board consists of the following members:
a Chair;
at least 2, and not more than 4, other members.

section.heading: Appointment of advisory board members etc.

content.p: Each advisory board member is to be appointed by the Minister by written instrument.
An advisory board member holds office for the period specified in the instrument of appointment. The period must not exceed 5 years.
Note: A board member is eligible for reappointment: see the Acts Interpretation Act 1901.
An advisory board member holds office on a part-time basis.
The Minister must ensure that the members of the AIP advisory board collectively possess experience or knowledge in all of the following fields:
economics;
industry;
project management;
procurement of goods or services.

section.heading: Vacancy in the membership of AIP advisory board

content.p: For the purposes of a reference in the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 to a vacancy in the membership of a body, there are taken to be 2 offices of members of the AIP advisory board in addition to the Chair of the AIP advisory board.

division.heading: Terms and conditions for advisory board members

content.p: An advisory board member is to be paid the remuneration that is determined by the Remuneration Tribunal. If no determination of that remuneration by the Tribunal is in operation, the member is to be paid the remuneration that is prescribed by the legislative rules.
An advisory board member is to be paid the allowances that are prescribed by the legislative rules.
(3) This section has effect subject to the Remuneration Tribunal Act 1973.
The Minister may grant leave of absence to an advisory board member on the terms and conditions that the Minister determines.

section.heading: Disclosure of interests to the Minister

content.p: An advisory board member must give written notice to the Minister of all interests, pecuniary or otherwise, that the member has or acquires and that conflict or could conflict with the proper performance of the member’s functions.

section.heading: Disclosure of interests to AIP advisory board

content.p: An advisory board member who has a direct or indirect pecuniary interest in a matter being considered or about to be considered by the AIP advisory board must disclose that interest to a meeting of the advisory board.
The disclosure must be made as soon as possible after the relevant facts have come to the advisory board member’s knowledge.
The disclosure must be recorded in the minutes of the meeting.
Unless the AIP advisory board otherwise determines, the advisory board member:
must not be present during any deliberation of the advisory board on the matter; and
must not take part in the making of a decision by the advisory board in relation to the matter.
For the purposes of making a determination under subsection (4), the advisory board member:
must not be present during any deliberation of the advisory board for the purpose of making the determination; and
must not take part in making the determination.
A determination under subsection (4) must be recorded in the minutes of the meeting of the advisory board.
An advisory board member may resign his or her appointment by giving the Minister a written resignation.
The resignation takes effect on the day it is received by the Minister or, if a later day is specified in the resignation, on that later day.
The Minister may terminate the appointment of an advisory board member.
The AIP advisory board must hold such meetings as are necessary for the performance of its functions.
The Chair of the AIP advisory board:
may convene a meeting; and
must convene a meeting if requested in writing by:
the Authority; or
the Minister.
The Chair of the AIP advisory board must preside at all meetings at which he or she is present.
If the Chair is not present at a meeting, the other advisory board members present must appoint one of themselves to preside.
At a meeting of the AIP advisory board, a quorum is constituted by a majority of the advisory board members.
However, if:
an advisory board member is required by section 93 not to be present during the deliberations, or to take part in any decision, of the advisory board with respect to a particular matter; and
when the advisory board member leaves the meeting concerned, there is no longer a quorum present;
the remaining advisory board members at the meeting constitute a quorum for the purpose of any deliberation or decision at that meeting with respect to that matter.
A question arising at a meeting is to be determined by a majority of the votes of the advisory board members present and voting.
The person presiding at a meeting has a deliberative vote and, in the event of an equality of votes, a casting vote.
Subject to this Division, the AIP advisory board may regulate proceedings at its meetings as it considers appropriate.
(2) For the purposes of section 33B of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901, the AIP advisory board is taken to have been established by this Act.
Note: Section 33B of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 contains extra rules about meetings by telephone etc.
The AIP advisory board must keep minutes of its meetings.
A person commits an offence if:
the person is, or has been, an entrusted official; and
the person has obtained protected information in the person’s capacity as an entrusted official; and
the person:
discloses the information to another person; or
uses the information; and
the disclosure or use is not:
authorised by a provision of this Part; or
in compliance with a requirement under a law of the Commonwealth; or
in compliance with a designated law of a State or Territory.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
Exceptions
Except where it is necessary to do so for the purposes of giving effect to this Act, an entrusted official is not to be required:
to produce to a court or tribunal a document containing protected information; or
to disclose protected information to a court or tribunal.
Designated law
(3) The legislative rules may declare that a specified law of a State or Territory is a designated law for the purposes of this section.

section.heading: Disclosure or use for the purposes of this Act etc.

content.p: An entrusted official may disclose or use protected information if:
the disclosure or use is for the purposes of this Act; or
the disclosure or use is for the purposes of the performance of the functions of the Authority; or
the disclosure or use is for the purposes of the performance of the functions of the AIP advisory board; or
the disclosure or use is in the course of the official’s employment or service as an entrusted official.
An entrusted official may disclose protected information to the Minister.
An entrusted official may disclose protected information to:
the Secretary of the Department; or
an officer of the Department who is authorised by the Secretary, in writing, for the purposes of this section;
if the disclosure is for the purposes of advising the Minister.
An entrusted official may disclose protected information to a Royal Commission.
The Authority may, by writing, impose conditions to be complied with in relation to protected information disclosed under subsection (1).
An instrument under subsection (2) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Disclosure to certain agencies, bodies and persons

content.p: Scope
This section applies if the Authority is satisfied that particular protected information will enable or assist any of the following agencies, bodies or persons:
the Australian Communications and Media Authority;
the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission;
the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority;
the Australian Securities and Investments Commission;
the National Competition Council;
the Productivity Commission;
the Australian Statistician;
the Commissioner of Taxation;
the Australian Competition Tribunal;
the Director of Public Prosecutions;
the Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre;
the Reserve Bank of Australia;
Industry Capability Network Limited (ACN 068 571 513);
(n) the Comptroller-General of Customs (within the meaning of the Customs Act 1901);
a State/Territory government body whose functions include a function that corresponds to a function of the Authority;
a designated State/Territory government body;
a designated professional disciplinary body;
to perform or exercise any of the functions or powers of the agency, body or person.
Disclosure
If an entrusted official is authorised by the Authority, in writing, for the purposes of this section, the official may disclose that protected information to the agency, body or person concerned.
The Authority may, by writing, impose conditions to be complied with in relation to protected information disclosed under subsection (2).
A person commits an offence if:
the person is subject to a condition under subsection (3); and
the person engages in conduct; and
the person’s conduct breaches the condition.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
An instrument under subsection (3) is not a legislative instrument.
Designated professional disciplinary bodies
A person commits an offence if:
the person is:
a designated professional disciplinary body; or
a member of a designated professional disciplinary body; and
protected information has been disclosed under subsection (2) to the body; and
the person:
discloses the information to another person; or
uses the information; and
the disclosure or use is not:
with the consent of the Authority; or
for the purpose of deciding whether or not to take disciplinary or other action; or
for the purpose of taking disciplinary or other action.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
Designated State/Territory government body
(7) The legislative rules may declare that a specified State/Territory government body is a designated State/Territory government body for the purposes of this section.
Designated professional disciplinary body
(8) The legislative rules may declare that a specified professional disciplinary body is a designated professional disciplinary body for the purposes of this section.
An entrusted official may disclose protected information that relates to the affairs of a person if:
the person has consented to the disclosure; and
the disclosure is in accordance with that consent.
An entrusted official may disclose protected information if it has already been lawfully made available to the public.
An entrusted official may disclose:
summaries of protected information; or
statistics derived from protected information;
if those summaries or statistics, as the case may be, are not likely to enable the identification of a person.

section.heading: Disclosure for purposes of law enforcement

content.p: Scope
This section applies if the Authority is satisfied that disclosure of particular protected information is reasonably necessary for:
the enforcement of the criminal law; or
the enforcement of a law imposing a pecuniary penalty; or
the protection of the public revenue.
Disclosure
The Authority may disclose that protected information to:
a Department, agency or authority of the Commonwealth, a State or a Territory; or
an Australian police force;
whose functions include that enforcement or protection, for the purposes of that enforcement or protection.
If an entrusted official is authorised by the Authority, in writing, for the purposes of this section, the official may disclose that protected information to:
a Department, agency or authority of the Commonwealth, a State or a Territory; or
an Australian police force;
whose functions include that enforcement or protection, for the purposes of that enforcement or protection.
Secondary disclosure and use
A person commits an offence if:
the person is, or has been, an employee or officer of:
a Department, agency or authority of the Commonwealth, a State or a Territory; or
an Australian police force; and
protected information has been disclosed under subsection (2) or (3) to the Department, agency, authority or police force, as the case may be; and
the person has obtained the information in the person’s capacity as an employee or officer of the Department, agency, authority or police force, as the case may be; and
the person:
discloses the information to another person; or
uses the information; and
the disclosure or use is not:
with the consent of the Authority; or
for the purpose of enforcing the criminal law; or
for the purpose of enforcing a law imposing a pecuniary penalty; or
for the purpose of protecting the public revenue.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
Conditions
The Authority may, by writing, impose conditions to be complied with in relation to protected information disclosed under subsection (2) or (3).
A person commits an offence if:
the person is subject to a condition under subsection (5); and
the person engages in conduct; and
the person’s conduct breaches the condition.
Penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years or 120 penalty units, or both.
An instrument under subsection (5) is not a legislative instrument.

section.heading: Review by the Administrative Review Tribunal

content.p: Applications may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of any of the following decisions of the Authority:

tr.td: A decision to make a determination under subsection 8(5).
A decision to make a declaration under subsection 9(3) or (5).
A decision to make a determination under subsection 10(2).
A decision to refuse to specify a day under paragraph 13(1)(c).
A decision to specify a day under paragraph 13(1)(c).
A decision to refuse to specify a later time under paragraph 17(1)(b).
A decision to specify a later time under paragraph 17(1)(b).
A decision under section 18, 19 or 20 to refuse to approve a draft AIP plan.
A decision to make a determination under subsection 25(4).
A decision to give a notice under subsection 57(2) or (3).
A decision to name a person in a report in accordance with subsection 57(4).
A decision to name a person under subsection 57(5).

section.heading: Operation of new relevant facility—constitutional basis

content.p: This Act does not apply to the operation of a new relevant facility in relation to a designated project except to the extent to which:
one or more constitutional corporations are responsible for operating the facility; or
the facility:

(i) is in one or more offshore areas (within the meaning of the Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Act 2006) and outside the Greater Sunrise special regime area (within the meaning of the Seas and Submerged Lands Act 1973); and
relates to the exercise of Australia’s sovereign rights in the exclusive economic zone or the continental shelf; or
the facility is for purposes related to trade or commerce:
between Australia and places outside Australia; or
among the States; or
within a Territory; or
between a State and a Territory; or
between 2 Territories; or
the facility is in a Territory; or
(e) the facility is in a Commonwealth place (within the meaning of the Commonwealth Places (Application of Laws) Act 1970).
Subsection (1) is to be disregarded in determining whether a project is a designated project.

section.heading: Concurrent operation of State and Territory laws

content.p: This Act is not intended to exclude or limit the operation of a law of a State or Territory that is capable of operating concurrently with this Act.
Commonwealth not to give preference

A function or power conferred by this Act must not be performed or exercised in such a way as to give preference (within the meaning of section 99 of the Constitution) to one State or part of a State over another State or part of a State.
Trade to be absolutely free

A function or power conferred by this Act must not be performed or exercised in such a way that the performance of the function, or the exercise of the power, would infringe section 92 of the Constitution.
Note: Section 92 of the Constitution requires trade among the States to be absolutely free.

section.heading: No interference with powers and functions of another jurisdiction

content.p: If:
apart from this subsection, this Act would operate so as to prevent or interfere with the exercise of the powers, or the performance of the functions or duties, of the government of a State; and
that operation would be invalid because of the Constitution;
this Act does not so operate.
If:

apart from this subsection, this Act would operate so as to prevent or interfere with the exercise of the powers, or the performance of the functions or duties, of the government of the Australian Capital Territory or the Northern Territory; and
that operation would be invalid because of the Constitution if it were assumed that the Territory were a State;
this Act does not so operate.

If the operation of this Act would result in an acquisition of property from a person otherwise than on just terms, the Commonwealth is liable to pay a reasonable amount of compensation to the person.

If the Commonwealth and the person do not agree on the amount of the compensation, the person may institute proceedings in a court of competent jurisdiction for the recovery from the Commonwealth of such reasonable amount of compensation as the court determines.
In this section:
acquisition of property has the same meaning as in paragraph 51(xxxi) of the Constitution.
just terms has the same meaning as in paragraph 51(xxxi) of the Constitution.

section.heading: Validity of transactions in contravention of Act

content.p: A contravention of this Act does not affect the validity of any transaction.
For the purposes of this Act, if a transaction has involved, or will involve, non-cash consideration, assume that the monetary value of that consideration has been, or will be, incurred.

section.heading: Translation of amounts into Australian currency

content.p: For the purposes of this Act, an amount in a foreign currency is to be translated into Australian currency.
The amount of foreign currency is to be translated to Australian currency at the exchange rate applicable at the relevant time.

section.heading: Law relating to legal professional privilege not affected

content.p: This Act does not affect the law relating to legal professional privilege.
None of the following:
the Minister;
the Authority;
a delegate of the Authority;
a member of the staff assisting the Authority;
a person assisting the Authority under section 81;
the AIP advisory board;
an advisory board member;
is liable to an action or other proceeding for damages for, or in relation to, an act or matter in good faith done or omitted to be done:
in the performance or purported performance of any function; or
in the exercise or purported exercise of any power;
conferred by this Act.
Before the end of the period of 5 years after the commencement of this section, the Minister must cause to be conducted a review of the operation of this Act.
A review under subsection (1) must be conducted in a manner that provides for wide public consultation.
The Minister must cause to be prepared a report of a review under subsection (1).
The Minister must cause copies of a report to be tabled in each House of the Parliament within 15 sittings days of that House after the completion of the preparation of the report.
The Minister may, by legislative instrument, make rules (legislative rules) prescribing matters:
(a) required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed by the legislative rules; or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act.
